overall_notes: Pair 2 cleanly hits Level 4 across all six scored categories. Alignment: every primary expectation (C3.1) has a named lesson activity (Stations A/B/C, exit-routine sticky notes), and the lesson explicitly bridges from Lesson 1 ('yesterday we READ IF-THEN code; today we WRITE it') and forward to Lesson 3 via the early-finisher tracing prompt. Pedagogical_depth: the missed-branch trap is a real, grade-level-specific Grade-2 conditional-coding misconception ('child writes IF the number is even, THEN clap and stops'), and recovery_moves branch by diagnosis (sentence frame for persistent misses, full coverage sweep, FALSE-branch praise for partial misses). Instructional_balance: lesson_specific_materials explicitly marks the puppets OPTIONAL with a no-puppet substitution ('teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected'); 12/25/13 timing is realistic for G2; differentiation includes a no-paper movement-learner path (act out actions). Clarity_voice: Inspector If anchors minds_on, action, and consolidation; all three success_criteria start with 'I can'; consolidation has a memorable two-branch chant frame 'IF ___, THEN ___. IF NOT ___, THEN ___.' that children carry between lessons. Mathematical_authenticity: lesson lets children invent their own conditions/actions at Station C and stretch into 3-branch IF-THEN-ELSE-IF, comparing strategies; vocabulary (condition, action, branch) is used precisely; the 'fork in the road' analogy carries conceptual meaning rather than rote procedure. Lesson_worksheet_consistency: worksheet's three parts each practise a named success criterion (Part 1 = pick a math condition / matching action; Part 2 = two branches; Part 3 = make your own), Part 3 deliberately varies format (open-ended generation as transfer, not rote repeat), image_assets mirror the station materials, and the teacher_notes call out the same missed-branch trap as the lesson's expanded_walkthrough.
